<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8" />
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
<title>Work Order Parts Availability — Fishbowl BI</title>
<!--
  Work Order Parts Availability (v1.2)
  ------------------------------------
  Oversight for work orders whose raw goods must be sourced. Traces each open
  WO's raw components, computes an availability picture per part+location group
  (available-to-pick stock, committed picks, incoming POs — including MO-linked
  express POs — and scheduled WO output), and derives a per-WO Ready date.

  Three views (tabs):
    • Work Orders — every WO in view with its Ready date and short raw goods.
    • Suggested Sequence — advisory reorder by earliest full material
      availability (material-only; no capacity/labour modelling).
    • Procurement — the buy/make shortage worklist with Create PO / Create MO.

  Built on the shared platform: fb-lib (FBLib.Settings/Common) + fb-styles.
  The availability engine + procurement worklist + PO/MO drawers are ported
  from Manufacturing/Production_Scheduling_v1.2.htm (psLoadAvailability et al.).
-->
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700;800&display=swap" rel="stylesheet" />
<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/moment.js/2.29.4/moment.min.js"></script>
<script>
    {% Script fb-lib %}
</script>
<style>
    {% Style fb-styles %}
</style>
<style>
    /* ============================================================
       REPORT-LOCAL STYLES
       fb-styles (above) owns the design tokens + all workspace chrome
       (.topbar .filterbar .tabs .kpi-tile .rpt-table .tbl-wrap .ms-*
       .spill .ps-btn .close-x .b* .toast-*). Everything below is either
       page layout glue or component CSS ported verbatim from
       Production_Scheduling_v1.2.htm for the drawers / procurement /
       availability tables (see the splice tokens).
       ============================================================ */
    html, body { height: 100%; }
    body { margin: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 100vh; overflow: hidden;
        background: var(--bg-1); color: var(--c-primary); font-family: var(--font); }

    /* Topbar */
    .topbar .subline { font-size: 12px; color: var(--c-tertiary); }
    .top-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; }

    /* Compact every button to the small type report-wide (saves vertical space —
       requested after prior reports had oversized chrome), but KEEP the icon glyphs
       at a legible size (15px, larger than the stock .sm 14px). */
    .ps-btn { height: 28px; padding: 0 10px; font-size: 12px; }
    .ps-btn.icon { width: 28px; }
    .ps-btn svg, .ps-btn.sm svg { width: 15px; height: 15px; }

    /* Tabs strip host + content panes */
    .tabs { padding: 0 22px; flex-shrink: 0; }
    /* Planner action buttons live inline on the tabs row (right-aligned) so the
       Planner pane doesn't need its own toolbar row. Hidden unless the Planner tab
       is active. */
    .plan-actions { margin-left: auto; display: none; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 8px; }
    .plan-actions.on { display: flex; }
    .app-shell { flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 0; }
    /* No TOP padding on the scroll container: a sticky table header pins at the
       container's content-box top, so any top padding leaves a gap above the header
       where scrolled rows bleed through. Push the content down with a child margin
       (which scrolls away) instead. */
    .tab-pane { display: none; flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto; padding: 0 22px 22px; }
    .tab-pane.active { display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
    .tab-pane > div { margin-top: 14px; }

    /* WO / Suggested tables use fb-styles .rpt-table; light wrapper for scroll. */
    .wa-tblwrap { width: 100%; }
    .wa-tblwrap table { width: 100%; }
    /* All data tables use the shared v1.2 dashboard tier (.tbl-wrap, fb-styles §30):
       navy uppercase sticky header, card border/radius/shadow. .tbl-fill makes the
       card fill its flex parent and scroll internally so the header stays pinned
       (mirrors Production_Scheduling_v1.2's .tbl-wrap.tbl-fill). */
    .tbl-fill { flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; }
    #workOrdersView { flex: 1; min-height: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
    .wa-th-sort { cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; user-select: none; }
    .wa-sub { font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--c-secondary); }
    .wa-prod { font-weight: 600; color: var(--c-primary); }
    .wa-move-up { color: var(--fb-success); font-weight: 700; }
    .wa-move-dn { color: var(--fb-warning); font-weight: 700; }
    .wa-move-same { color: var(--c-tertiary); }
    .wa-risk-row td { background: #FBF1F3; }
    /* Editable planned-start date in the Planner's Planned-schedule table. */
    .wa-date { font: inherit; font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--c-primary); padding: 2px 4px;
        border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: 5px; background: #fff; vertical-align: middle; }
    .wa-date:hover { border-color: var(--fb-blue); }
    .wa-date:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--fb-blue); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(45,156,219,.15); }
    .wa-empty { text-align: center; color: var(--c-tertiary); padding: 60px 20px; font-size: 14px; }
    .wa-summary { font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--c-secondary); margin-bottom: 12px; display: flex;
        gap: 16px; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; }
    .wa-summary b { color: var(--c-primary); }
    .wa-loading { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; flex-direction: column;
        gap: 10px; height: 50vh; color: var(--c-secondary); font-size: 13px; }

    /* Planner — two-pane what-if scheduler (Current | Planned). */
    #suggestedView { flex: 1; min-height: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
    /* Planner action buttons (Plan all / Revert all / Apply) render inline on the
       tabs row (.plan-actions above), not in a per-pane toolbar — reclaims a row of
       vertical space. */
    .plan-wrap { display: flex; gap: 16px; align-items: stretch; flex: 1; min-height: 0; }
    .plan-col { flex: 1; min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-height: 0; }
    /* Fixed header height so both column titles line up their tables identically. */
    .plan-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin-bottom: 8px; min-height: 24px; }
    .plan-head h3 { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 800; margin: 0; color: var(--c-primary); }
    .plan-scroll { flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-card); }
    /* table-layout:fixed + a colgroup pins column widths, so a long Ready/Reason cell
       (which can list several WOs) wraps WITHIN its column instead of stretching it
       past the scroll area. .pl-wrap columns wrap; others stay single-line. */
    .plan-scroll table { width: 100%; table-layout: fixed; }
    .plan-scroll td { overflow: hidden; }
    .plan-scroll td.pl-wrap { white-space: normal; overflow-wrap: anywhere; vertical-align: top; }
    .plan-scroll th { position: relative; }
    .pl-c-date { white-space: nowrap; }
    /* Drag handle straddling each column border (all but the last) to resize columns. */
    .pl-rz { position: absolute; top: 0; right: -3px; width: 7px; height: 100%; cursor: col-resize; z-index: 4; }
    .pl-rz:hover { background: rgba(213, 228, 232, .5); }

    /* Filter strip pieces (fb-styles supplies .filterbar/.fchip/.ms-*). */
    .filterbar { flex-shrink: 0; }
    .fl-lbl { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--c-tertiary); text-transform: uppercase;
        letter-spacing: .04em; margin-right: 2px; }
    .fl-search { height: 30px; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--r-btn);
        padding: 0 10px; font-family: inherit; font-size: 13px; color: var(--c-primary); background: #fff;
        outline: none; width: 150px; }
    .fl-search:focus { border-color: var(--fb-blue); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(45,156,219,.15); }
    #lgMs { min-width: 200px; }
    .srch-ms { min-width: 165px; }

    /* ── Ported CSS: procurement + shared table cells ── */
            .tbl-wrap tbody tr { cursor:pointer; transition:.1s; }
        .tbl-wrap td .wo { font-family:var(--mono); font-weight:700; color:var(--link); }
        .rowflags { display:inline-flex; gap:4px; }

        /* Procurement tab — vendor groups + shared cell styling. */
        .proc-vgrp { margin-bottom:16px; }
        .proc-vhead { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; font-size:12px; font-weight:700;
            text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.03em; color:var(--c-secondary); margin:0 0 5px; }
        .proc-vcount { font-size:11px; font-weight:700; color:#fff; background:var(--fb-neutral); border-radius:var(--r-pill); padding:1px 7px; }
        .proc-desc { font-size:11.5px; color:var(--c-secondary); }
        /* Compact procurement rows: description gets its own column (single-line,
           ellipsised) and the row padding is tightened to save vertical space. */
        .tbl-wrap.proc-tbl tbody td { padding:5px 12px; }
        .tbl-wrap.proc-tbl thead th { padding:7px 12px; }
        .proc-desccell { max-width:240px; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; color:var(--c-secondary); font-size:11.5px; }
        /* Blocked-work-orders cell — table-like column alignment WITHOUT a nested
           <table>: one CSS grid with four cells per WO (scheduled start · WO# ·
           finished good · qty) so values line up down the column. Capped to 5 rows
           (.blk-cap) and expanded on click via psBlkToggle. */
        .proc-blk { display:grid; grid-template-columns:auto auto minmax(0,1fr) auto; gap:2px 10px; align-items:baseline; line-height:18px; }
        .proc-blk.blk-cap { max-height:100px; overflow:hidden; }
        .proc-blk .bwo { font-family:var(--mono); font-weight:700; font-size:11.5px; color:var(--link); text-decoration:none; white-space:nowrap; }
        .proc-blk .bwo:hover { text-decoration:underline; }
        .proc-blk .bdate { font-size:11px; color:var(--c-secondary); white-space:nowrap; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; }
        .proc-blk .bfg { font-size:11.5px; color:var(--c-secondary); overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap; min-width:0; }
        .proc-blk .bqty { font-size:11.5px; color:var(--c-secondary); text-align:right; white-space:nowrap; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; }
        .blk-toggle { cursor:pointer; }
        .blk-more { margin-top:4px; font-size:10.5px; color:var(--link); user-select:none; }
        /* To Purchase / To Manufacture tab switch (sub-tabs within the
           Procurement view — an underline tab strip like the top view tabs). */
        .proc-tabbar { display:flex; gap:2px; align-items:flex-end; margin-bottom:16px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--border); }
        .proc-tab { height:38px; padding:0 16px; border:none; background:transparent; color:var(--c-secondary);
            font-size:14px; font-weight:700; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:8px;
            border-bottom:2px solid transparent; margin-bottom:-1px; cursor:pointer; font-family:inherit; transition:.15s; }
        .proc-tab:hover { color:var(--c-primary); }
        .proc-tab.active { color:var(--fb-blue); border-bottom-color:var(--fb-blue); }
        .proc-tabn { font-size:11px; font-weight:700; background:var(--bg-2); color:var(--c-secondary);
            border-radius:var(--r-pill); padding:1px 8px; min-width:20px; text-align:center; }
        .proc-tab.active .proc-tabn { background:#DEEAF4; color:var(--fb-blue); }
        /* Per-tab header row (description + tab-level action button) + subtitle. */
        .proc-subhead { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; flex-wrap:wrap; margin:0 0 12px; }
        .proc-subtitle { font-size:12px; color:var(--c-secondary); margin:0 0 12px; }
        /* Create MO drawer form. */
        .mo-form { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:10px; }
        .mo-form label, .mo-form .mo-cf { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:3px; }
        .mo-form label > span:first-child, .mo-cf-lbl { font-size:11px; font-weight:700; color:var(--c-secondary); }
        .mo-form input, .mo-form select, .mo-form textarea { box-sizing:border-box; height:34px;
            border:1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius:var(--r-btn); padding:0 8px; font-size:13px;
            font-family:inherit; color:var(--c-primary); background:#fff; outline:none; }
        .mo-form textarea { height:auto; padding:6px 8px; resize:vertical; }
        .mo-form input:focus, .mo-form select:focus, .mo-form textarea:focus { border-color:var(--fb-blue); box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(45,156,219,.15); }

    /* ── Ported CSS: detail drawer chrome + alerts + availability table ── */
            /* Detail drawer (right slide-in) */
        .scrim { position:fixed; inset:0; background:rgba(16,16,16,.35); opacity:0; pointer-events:none; transition:.2s; z-index:10001; }
        .scrim.on { opacity:1; pointer-events:auto; }
        .detail { position:fixed; top:0; right:0; bottom:0; width:560px; max-width:94vw; background:#fff; z-index:10002;
            box-shadow:var(--sh3); transform:translateX(100%); transition:transform .22s cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1);
            display:flex; flex-direction:column; }
        .detail.on { transform:translateX(0); }
        /* WO detail drawer is wider than the shared 560px so the raw-goods table's
           ETA column isn't scrolled off-screen. */
        #detailPanel { width:760px; }
        .detail-head { padding:16px 20px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--border); }
        /* Header is a two-column row: the text block (WO#, title, sub, pills) on
           the left and the action stack on the right, both top-aligned — so the
           title stays at the top and the buttons never push it down. */
        .detail-head .top { display:flex; align-items:flex-start; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; }
        .detail-head-main { flex:1; min-width:0; }
        /* Top-right action stack — close-X on top, then the compact record actions.
           The action buttons stretch to the widest (Open in Fishbowl) so Timeline
           matches its width; the close-X keeps its own square size, top-right. */
        .detail-actions { display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:stretch; gap:6px; flex-shrink:0; }
        .detail-actions .close-x { align-self:flex-end; }
        .detail-actions .ps-btn { justify-content:center; }
        /* .ps-btn.sm ships from fb-styles (§23). */
        .detail-head .wo { font-family:var(--mono); font-weight:700; font-size:13px; color:var(--link); }
        .detail-head h2 { font-size:19px; font-weight:800; margin:0; letter-spacing:-.01em; color:var(--c-primary); }
        .detail-head .sub { font-size:13px; color:var(--c-secondary); margin-top:3px; }
        /* flex:1 + min-height:0 is required so the body actually scrolls on short
           (low-resolution) screens — without min-height:0 a flex child refuses to
           shrink below its content height and the overflow never engages, hiding
           the lower sections (raw goods, FG tracking, footer buttons). */
        .detail-body { padding:16px 20px; overflow-y:auto; overflow-x:hidden; flex:1 1 auto; min-height:0; }
        /* .ps-btn.success ships from fb-styles (§23). */
        .dsec { margin-bottom:16px; }
        .dsec h4 { font-size:11px; font-weight:700; text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.05em; color:var(--c-tertiary); margin:0 0 10px; }
        /* Section header with a trailing action/edit affordance (pencil or Finish WO). */
        .dsec h4.dsec-h { display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:8px; min-height:28px; }
        .dsec h4.dsec-h .ps-btn { text-transform:none; letter-spacing:normal; font-weight:600; }
        .ps-edit { width:24px; height:24px; border-radius:var(--r-btn); border:1px solid var(--border); background:#fff;
            color:var(--c-secondary); display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; cursor:pointer; flex-shrink:0; }
        .ps-edit:hover { background:var(--bg-1); border-color:var(--fb-neutral); color:var(--fb-blue); }
        .ps-edit svg { width:13px; height:13px; }
        .dgrid { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:12px 16px; }
        .dfield .k { font-size:11px; color:var(--c-secondary); font-weight:600; margin-bottom:2px; }
        .dfield .v { font-size:14px; font-weight:600; color:var(--c-primary); }
        /* Inline date/time + category editor at the top of the WO drawer. */
        /* Two-column grid: [Start][Finish] on row 1, [Category][Apply+Cancel] on
           row 2 — so Category matches the Start field width and the buttons sit
           squarely under the Finish field. */
        .dedit { display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:10px; align-items:end; }
        .dedit label { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:3px; font-size:11px; font-weight:600; color:var(--c-secondary); min-width:0; }
        .dedit input, .dedit select { width:100%; box-sizing:border-box; height:34px; border:1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius:var(--r-btn);
            padding:0 8px; font-size:13px; font-family:inherit; color:var(--c-primary); background:#fff; outline:none; }
        .dedit input:focus, .dedit select:focus { border-color:var(--fb-blue); box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(45,156,219,.15); }
        /* Apply + Cancel share the row-2 cell under Finish, side by side. */
        .dedit-actions { display:flex; gap:8px; }
        .dedit-actions .ps-btn { flex:1; height:34px; }
        /* .close-x base (28px) ships from fb-styles (§33); this report's
           drawers use the larger 32px variant everywhere. */
        .close-x { width:32px; height:32px; }
        .close-x svg { width:18px; height:18px; }
        .dprogress { height:8px; background:var(--bg-2); border-radius:var(--r-pill); overflow:hidden; margin-top:6px; }
        .dprogress div { height:100%; background:var(--fb-blue); border-radius:var(--r-pill); }
        .alert-box { display:flex; gap:10px; padding:11px 13px; border-radius:var(--r-card); margin-bottom:8px; font-size:12.5px; font-weight:600; }
        .alert-box svg { width:18px; height:18px; flex-shrink:0; margin-top:1px; }

        /* Component availability (detail drawer) — collapsible header + raw-goods table. */
        .avail-head { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; cursor:pointer; padding:8px 10px;
            background:var(--bg-1); border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:var(--r-card); }
        .avail-head:hover { background:var(--bg-2); }
        .avail-chevron { display:inline-flex; color:var(--c-secondary); flex-shrink:0; }
        .avail-chevron svg { width:16px; height:16px; }
        .avail-note { font-size:11px; color:var(--c-tertiary); margin-left:auto; text-align:right; }
        /* Raw-goods table: shared .tbl-wrap dashboard tier (§30 — navy uppercase
           sticky header) + compact drawer overrides. Scrolls within its own capped
           box so a long parts list never pushes the drawer footer off-screen. */
        .avail-parts.tbl-wrap { margin-top:8px; max-height:300px; }
        .avail-parts.tbl-wrap table { font-size:12px; }
        .avail-parts.tbl-wrap thead th { padding:6px 8px; font-size:10px; }
        .avail-parts.tbl-wrap tbody td { padding:7px 8px; vertical-align:top; }
        .avail-parts th.num, .avail-parts td.num { text-align:right; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; }
        .avail-parts td.num { font-family:inherit; }   /* body font, not the tbl-wrap mono, for the mixed status/ETA cells */
        /* WO detail drawer: make the raw-goods table fill the remaining drawer height
           (one scroll region using the full space) instead of a fixed 300px box that
           forced a nested scrollbar. */
        .detail-body-fill { display:flex; flex-direction:column; }
        .detail-body-fill .dsec-fill { flex:1 1 auto; min-height:0; display:flex; flex-direction:column; margin-bottom:0; }
        .detail-body-fill .dsec-fill > h4 { flex-shrink:0; }
        .detail-body-fill .avail-parts.tbl-wrap { flex:1 1 auto; min-height:0; max-height:none; }
        /* Availability cell — allow its content to wrap within the cell
           instead of overflowing the drawer; right-aligned to match the
           numeric columns. */
        .avail-parts .apstat { display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:4px; align-items:center; justify-content:flex-end; }
        .avail-parts .apn { font-weight:700; color:var(--c-primary); }
        .avail-parts .apd { font-size:10.5px; color:var(--c-secondary); max-width:150px; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis; white-space:nowrap; }

        .ps-empty { text-align:center; color:var(--c-tertiary); padding:60px 20px; font-size:14px; }
        .hint { font-size:11.5px; color:var(--c-tertiary); display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:5px; }
        .hint svg { width:14px; height:14px; }

    /* ── Ported CSS: Create MO / Create PO drawer z-index tiers ── */
            /* Create MO drawer (Procurement tab) — sits above the detail drawer. */
        #moScrim { z-index:10007; }
        #moPanel { z-index:10008; width:560px; }
        /* Create PO drawer (Procurement tab). */
        #poScrim { z-index:10009; }
        #poPanel { z-index:10010; width:600px; }

    /* ── Ported CSS: PO/MO drawer banner + line-item table ── */
            .pf-banner { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px; flex-wrap:wrap;
            padding:11px 13px; border-radius:var(--r-card); border-left:4px solid var(--fb-neutral);
            background:var(--bg-1); margin-bottom:14px; }
        .pf-banner.ok   { border-left-color:#A9CDBA; background:#F1F7F3; }
        .pf-banner.warn { border-left-color:#EBC49B; background:#FBF4EC; }
        .pf-banner.late { border-left-color:#D9A4B2; background:#F7ECEF; }
        .pf-banner .pf-summary { flex:1; display:flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:6px 10px; align-items:center; }
        .pf-banner .pf-actions { display:flex; gap:6px; align-items:center; flex-shrink:0; }
        .pf-banner .ps-btn.primary:disabled { opacity:.5; cursor:not-allowed; }
        .pf-blocker-list { margin:2px 0 14px 18px; padding:0; font-size:12px; color:#8A1E30; }
        .pf-blocker-list li { margin:3px 0; }
        .pf-steps { display:inline-flex; flex-wrap:wrap; gap:4px; }

        /* Raw-goods / FG table inside the finish drawer — reuse the
           .avail-parts look (scroll box + sticky header). */
        .pf-table { width:100%; border-collapse:collapse; font-size:12px; }
        .pf-tablewrap { margin-top:8px; border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:var(--r-card); max-height:320px; overflow:auto; }
        .pf-table th { background:var(--bg-1); color:var(--c-secondary); text-align:left; font-size:10px; font-weight:700;
            text-transform:uppercase; letter-spacing:.04em; padding:6px 8px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);
            position:sticky; top:0; z-index:1; }
        .pf-table td { padding:7px 8px; border-bottom:1px solid var(--bg-2); vertical-align:top; }
        .pf-table tr:last-child td { border-bottom:none; }
        .pf-table td.num, .pf-table th.num { text-align:right; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; }
        .pf-table input[type="number"] { width:80px; height:26px; padding:2px 6px; border:1px solid var(--border-strong);
            border-radius:5px; font-family:inherit; font-size:12px; text-align:right; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;
            background:#fff; color:var(--c-primary); }
        .pf-table input[type="number"]:focus { outline:none; border-color:var(--fb-blue); box-shadow:0 0 0 2px rgba(45,156,219,.15); }
        .pf-table input[type="number"].dirty { border-color:var(--fb-warning); background:#FBF4EC; }
        /* Scrap-location hint under the Scrapped input. */

        <h3>Availability engine</h3>
        <p>Each work order's raw components are matched against, in order: stock committed to that WO on a pick, shared available-to-pick stock in its location group, purchase orders raised for the WO's manufacture order (express POs), blanket purchase orders, and finished-good output scheduled from other work orders. Stock is allocated FIFO in scheduled-start order, so an earlier WO gets first claim on shared stock.</p>
        <ul>
            <li><b>Buildable now</b> — every component is available today.</li>
            <li><b>Waiting</b> — fully sourced, but the binding component arrives on a future PO/WO date (the Ready date). A padlock marks a date secured by an MO-linked PO.</li>
            <li><b>Contested</b> — stock physically exists, but earlier-scheduled WOs have first claim; resequencing (not purchasing) would secure it.</li>
            <li><b>Unmet</b> — a genuine shortage that needs a PO or MO.</li>
        </ul>
        <h3>Planner</h3>
        <p>A two-pane what-if scheduler. The left pane is the current schedule; click <b>Plan</b> on a work order to move it to its earliest material-ready date. Planned changes stage on the right, where the scenario re-runs the availability engine and cascades staged dependencies (a consumer never starts before its producer finishes). <b>Plan all recommended</b> stages every buildable WO at once; <b>Revert</b> removes a staged change. When you're happy, <b>Apply</b> writes the new start/finish dates for every planned work order to Fishbowl. This is <b>material-only</b> — it does not model machine capacity or labour.</p>
        <h3>Business calendar & scheduling maths</h3>
        <p>When the Planner proposes a new start and finish for a work order, it uses the business calendar set in <b>Settings</b> (business days plus opening hours, saved org-wide by an administrator). It works in whole days, like a wall calendar — it decides which <i>days</i> the build runs on, not the clock time.</p>
        <ul>
            <li><b>Start day</b> — the work order moves to the earliest day its materials are ready (never in the past). If that day isn't a working day, it rolls forward to the next one.</li>
            <li><b>How long it takes</b> — the build time comes from the BOM's estimated time × the quantity being built. That total is spread across working days, giving each day one full "opening hours" worth of capacity (for example, 8:00–17:00 = 9 hours a day). Weekends and any non-working days are simply skipped.</li>
            <li><b>Finish day</b> — in plain terms: total build hours ÷ hours per working day, rounded up, tells you how many working days the build needs. The finish lands that many working days out from the start (a job that fits in one day finishes the same day; anything longer carries onto the following working day, jumping over weekends and days off).</li>
            <li><b>Knock-on effects</b> — if one work order feeds another, the consumer is pushed to start no earlier than the day after its producer finishes (again snapped to a working day), and its own length is worked out the same way.</li>
        </ul>
        <p><b>Worth knowing:</b> this is deliberately simple. It assumes each build gets a whole working day at a time, doesn't split a part-day, and doesn't limit how many work orders share the same day (no machine or labour capacity). It also assumes the BOM's estimated time is per unit. And when you <b>Apply</b>, only the dates change — each work order keeps its existing time of day. Work orders without an estimated build time keep their original calendar length.</p>
        <h3>Procurement</h3>
        <p>The genuine shortages across the work orders in view, split into <b>To Purchase</b> (grouped by default vendor) and <b>To Manufacture</b> (parts with a BOM). Create PO / Create MO write directly to Fishbowl via the REST API; supply is created in the same location group the shortage sits in so the engine can match it. Creating a PO does not email the vendor.</p>

               wo.id AS wo_id, wo.num AS wo_num, wo.statusid AS wo_status,
               moitem.description AS description,
               COALESCE(wo.datescheduled, moitem.datescheduled) AS date_scheduled,
               COALESCE(wo.datescheduledtostart, moitem.datescheduledtostart) AS date_scheduled_start,
               wo.datefinished AS date_finished,
               wo.qtyTarget AS qty_target,
               wo.locationgroupid AS location_group_id,
               lg.name AS site_name,
               wo.priorityId AS priority_id,
               COALESCE(pr.name, '') AS priority_name,
               COALESCE(bom.estimatedDuration, 0) * COALESCE(wo.qtyTarget, 0) AS estimated_duration,
               (SELECT woitem.uomid FROM woitem WHERE woitem.woid = wo.id AND woitem.typeid = 10 LIMIT 1) AS out_uom,
               (SELECT part.num FROM woitem LEFT JOIN part ON woitem.partid = part.id
                 WHERE woitem.woid = wo.id AND woitem.typeid = 10 LIMIT 1) AS part_num
        FROM wo
        LEFT JOIN moitem ON wo.moitemid = moitem.id
        LEFT JOIN mo ON moitem.moid = mo.id
        LEFT JOIN bom ON moitem.bomid = bom.id
        LEFT JOIN locationgroup lg ON lg.id = wo.locationgroupid
        LEFT JOIN priority pr ON pr.id = wo.priorityId
        WHERE wo.num IS NOT NULL
          AND wo.statusid IN (10, 30, 40)
          AND moitem.typeid = 50` + lgWo + `
          AND (mo.statusid NOT IN (60, 70, 80)
               OR COALESCE(wo.datefinished, moitem.datescheduled) >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 180 DAY))
        ORDER BY mo.num, wo.num
    `;

    // Staging edges (producer WO → consumer WO within ONE MO) linked STRUCTURALLY via
    // the MO's moitem parentid tree, NOT by matching part name across the MO. A
    // multi-config MO (≥2 builds of the same finished good) has every stage's part
    // twice, so part-name matching cross-links the chains and makes planning one WO
    // cascade to unrelated WOs. The tree: a sub-assembly build header (producer_mi,
    // typeid=50) has parentid = the consuming component line (comp_line, typeid=20),
    // whose parentid = the consumer's build header (consumer_mi, typeid=50). Each WO
    // joins its header via wo.moItemId. Output columns unchanged (wo_id=consumer,
    // staging_wo_id=producer, part_num=consumed component). See the memory reference.
    const depQuery = `
        SELECT DISTINCT consumer_wo.id AS wo_id, consumer_wo.num AS wo_num,
               producer_wo.id AS staging_wo_id, producer_wo.num AS staging_wo_num,
               COALESCE(producer_wo.datescheduled, producer_mi.datescheduled) AS staging_wo_finish,
               COALESCE(consumer_wo.datescheduledtostart, consumer_mi.datescheduledtostart) AS wo_start,
               comp_part.num AS part_num
        FROM moitem producer_mi
        INNER JOIN moitem comp_line   ON comp_line.id   = producer_mi.parentid AND comp_line.typeid   = 20
        INNER JOIN moitem consumer_mi ON consumer_mi.id = comp_line.parentid   AND consumer_mi.typeid = 50
        INNER JOIN mo ON mo.id = producer_mi.moid
        INNER JOIN wo producer_wo ON producer_wo.moitemid = producer_mi.id
        INNER JOIN wo consumer_wo ON consumer_wo.moitemid = consumer_mi.id
        LEFT  JOIN part comp_part ON comp_part.id = comp_line.partid
        WHERE producer_mi.typeid = 50
          AND producer_wo.statusid IN (10, 30, 40) AND consumer_wo.statusid IN (10, 30, 40)
          AND producer_wo.id != consumer_wo.id AND mo.statusid < 60
    `;

    const moQuery = `
        SELECT DISTINCT mo.num AS mo_num, mo.id AS mo_id, mo.statusid AS mo_status,
               mo.datescheduled AS mo_date_scheduled, fg_part.num AS part_num,
               moitem.description AS description, moitem.qtytofulfill AS qty, bom.num AS bom_num,
               so.num AS so_num, so.customerpo AS customer_po, customer.name AS customer_name
        FROM mo
        LEFT JOIN moitem ON moitem.moid = mo.id AND moitem.typeid = 50 AND moitem.parentid IS NULL
        LEFT JOIN bom ON moitem.bomid = bom.id
        LEFT JOIN moitem AS fg_moitem ON fg_moitem.parentid = moitem.id AND fg_moitem.typeid = 10
        LEFT JOIN part AS fg_part ON fg_moitem.partid = fg_part.id
        LEFT JOIN soitem ON moitem.soitemid = soitem.id
        LEFT JOIN so ON soitem.soid = so.id
        LEFT JOIN customer ON so.customerid = customer.id
        WHERE mo.id IN (
            SELECT DISTINCT mo.id FROM wo
            LEFT JOIN moitem ON wo.moitemid = moitem.id
            LEFT JOIN mo ON moitem.moid = mo.id
            WHERE wo.num IS NOT NULL AND wo.statusid IN (10, 30, 40)` + lgWo + `
              AND (mo.statusid NOT IN (60, 70, 80)
                   OR COALESCE(wo.datefinished, moitem.datescheduled) >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 180 DAY)))
        ORDER BY mo.num
    `;

    try {
        allWorkOrders = JSON.parse(runQuery(woQuery)) || [];
        debugLog('success', 'Loaded ' + allWorkOrders.length + ' work orders');
        try { stagingDependencies = JSON.parse(runQuery(depQuery)) || []; } catch (e) { stagingDependencies = []; debugLog('warn', 'staging deps failed: ' + (e && e.message)); }
        try { manufacturingOrders = JSON.parse(runQuery(moQuery)) || []; } catch (e) { manufacturingOrders = []; debugLog('warn', 'MO query failed: ' + (e && e.message)); }
        psLoadAvailability();
        // Snapshot the baseline (original dates + availability) for the Planner's
        // current-vs-planned comparison, and drop any stale planned changes.
        allWorkOrders.forEach(w => { w._start0 = w.date_scheduled_start; w._finish0 = w.date_scheduled; w._avBase = w._av; });
        plannedManual.clear(); scenarioEff = new Map(); scenarioAvById = new Map();
        populateSearchFilters();   // refresh WO # / Raw Good / Finished Good option lists
        applyFilters();
        render();
    } catch (e) {
        setStatus('Failed to load work orders — ' + (e && e.message));
        showToast('Failed to load work orders: ' + (e && e.message), 'error', 8000);
        debugLog('error', 'loadWorkOrders failed: ' + (e && e.message));
    }
}

function waContestInline(wo) {

    const shown = parts.slice(0, 3).map(p => {

// The item(s) that GATE a WO (meeting requirement). Also names the PRECEDING work
// order when the gate is a staged sub-assembly built by another WO. The longest-
// lead item (staged or incoming) is the binding gate for a waiting WO.
function waGatePart(wo) { let best = null; waParts(wo).forEach(p => { if (p.nonInv) return; if (p.availableBy && (!best || p.availableBy > best.availableBy)) best = p; }); return best; }

function readyChip(wo) {

function readySortVal(wo) {
    const ai = psAvInfo(wo); const rank = { now: 0, tie: 1, contended: 1, wait: 2, unmet: 3, done: 4 };
    const r = ai ? (rank[ai.state] != null ? rank[ai.state] : 5) : 5;
    const d = (wo._av && wo._av._buildable) ? moment(wo._av._buildable).valueOf() : Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;

// Product sort key: the finished good (description, else part number), so the same
// FG built across multiple MOs/WOs lands on adjacent rows (Michael's request).
function waProductKey(w) { return String(w.description || w.part_num || '').toLowerCase(); }
// Ascending comparator for a given sort mode (tie-broken by WO #). sortWorkOrders
// reverses it for descending.
function sortCmpFor(mode) {
    if (mode === 'scheduled') return (a, b) => (moment(a.date_scheduled_start).valueOf() || 0) - (moment(b.date_scheduled_start).valueOf() || 0) || String(a.wo_num).localeCompare(String(b.wo_num));

    if (mode === 'wonum') return (a, b) => String(a.wo_num).localeCompare(String(b.wo_num));

/* ============================================================
   PLANNER — two-pane what-if scheduler
   Left = current schedule. Right = planned (staged) changes. "Plan" a WO moves
   it to its earliest material-ready date; the scenario re-runs the availability
   engine on the planned dates (cascading staged dependencies both ways) so
   knock-on effects show immediately. "Apply" commits every planned WO's new
   start/finish to Fishbowl via SaveWorkOrderRq (the proven PS v1.2 write path).
   ============================================================ */
let plannedManual = new Map();   // wo_id -> { start:'YYYY-MM-DD', finish:'YYYY-MM-DD' }  (user-staged)
let scenarioEff = new Map();     // wo_id -> { start:moment, finish:moment, auto:bool }    (manual + cascade)
let scenarioAvById = new Map();  // wo_id -> _av computed under the scenario
let planApplying = false;

function woById(id) { return allWorkOrders.find(w => String(w.wo_id) === String(id)); }
function planDur(w) { const s = moment(w._start0), f = moment(w._finish0); const d = f.startOf('day').diff(s.startOf('day'), 'days'); return (isNaN(d) || d < 0) ? 0 : d; }
// Availability meta derived from an explicit _av (base or scenario), mirroring psAvInfo.
function avStateFromAv(w, av) {
    if (!psAvailReady || !av) return null;
    if (parseInt(w.wo_status, 10) === 40 || psMoFinished(w)) return { label: 'Fulfilled', tone: 'success', state: 'done' };
    if (av._unmet) return { label: 'Attention required', tone: 'critical', state: 'unmet' };
    // Contested / tie are BUILDABLE (free stock exists) but shared with another open
    // WO — caution, not the red "blocked" treatment.
    if (av._tie) return { label: 'Buildable — tie', tone: 'caution', state: 'tie' };
    if (av._contended) return { label: 'Buildable — stock contested', tone: 'caution', state: 'contended' };
    if (av._buildableNow) return { label: 'Buildable now', tone: 'success', state: 'now' };
    return { label: 'Buildable ' + psFmtDate(av._buildable), tone: 'active', state: 'wait' };
}
function readyChipFromAv(w, av) {
    const ai = avStateFromAv(w, av);
    if (!ai) return '<span style="color:var(--c-tertiary)">—</span>';
    if (ai.state === 'unmet') return psSpill('critical', 'Att Req\'d');
    if (ai.state === 'tie') return psSpill('caution', 'Tie', { title: waTieTitle(av) });
    if (ai.state === 'contended') return psSpill('caution', 'Contested');
    if (ai.state === 'now') return psSpill('success', 'Now');
    if (ai.state === 'done') return psSpill('success', 'Fulfilled');
    return psSpill('active', psFmtDate(av._buildable));
}
// The scenario _av in effect for a WO (planned if computed this session, else baseline).

function psSaveWODates(woNum, newStartDate, newEndDate) {

        const woResponse = JSON.parse(runApiRequest('GetWorkOrderRq', JSON.stringify({ GetWorkOrderRq: { WorkOrderNumber: woNum } })));
        if (woResponse.GetWorkOrderRs && woResponse.GetWorkOrderRs.statusCode === 1000 && woResponse.GetWorkOrderRs.WO) {

            const os = moment(wo.DateScheduledToStart), oe = moment(wo.DateScheduled);
            const ns = moment(newStartDate).hour(os.hour() || 6).minute(os.minute()).second(os.second() || 0);

/* ============================================================
   BUSINESS CALENDAR (admin setting, org-wide) + working-time maths
   Business days + opening hours drive how the Planner turns each BOM's
   estimated build time (bom.estimatedDuration × qty, minutes) into a
   work-order start/finish, spreading the build across working days/hours.
   ============================================================ */
// Resolved business config (master over defaults). days = moment weekday nums
// (0=Sun … 6=Sat); minsPerDay = opening-hours window in minutes.
function bizCfg() {
    let days = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], start = '08:00', end = '17:00';
    try {
        const d = FBLib.Settings.resolve('bizDays'); if (Array.isArray(d) && d.length) days = d.map(Number);
        const s = FBLib.Settings.resolve('bizStart'); if (s) start = s;
        const e = FBLib.Settings.resolve('bizEnd'); if (e) end = e;
    } catch (_) {}
    const sp = String(start).split(':'), ep = String(end).split(':');
    let mins = ((+ep[0] || 0) * 60 + (+ep[1] || 0)) - ((+sp[0] || 0) * 60 + (+sp[1] || 0));
    if (!(mins > 0)) mins = 8 * 60;
    return { days: new Set(days.map(Number)), start: start, end: end, minsPerDay: mins };
}
// Advance to the next business day (inclusive). Returns a day-floored clone.
function waNextBizDay(m) { const cfg = bizCfg(); const c = m.clone().startOf('day'); if (!cfg.days.size) return c; let g = 0; while (!cfg.days.has(c.day()) && g++ < 400) c.add(1, 'day'); return c; }
// Finish DATE for a build of `minutes` starting on startYMD, spread across
// business days at minsPerDay each (day granularity — matches the WO date model).
function waWorkingFinish(startYMD, minutes) {
    const cfg = bizCfg();
    let cur = waNextBizDay(moment(startYMD));
    if (!minutes || minutes <= 0 || !cfg.days.size) return cur;
    let remaining = minutes - cfg.minsPerDay, g = 0;   // the first business day consumes one day's capacity
    while (remaining > 1e-6 && g++ < 3000) { cur.add(1, 'day'); while (!cfg.days.has(cur.day())) cur.add(1, 'day'); remaining -= cfg.minsPerDay; }
    return cur;
}
// Planned finish for a WO from a start moment: working-time from the BOM's
// estimated build minutes when known, else the WO's original calendar span.
function waPlanFinish(w, startM) {
    const mins = Number(w && w.estimated_duration) || 0;
    if (mins > 0) return waWorkingFinish(startM.format('YYYY-MM-DD'), mins);
    return startM.clone().add(planDur(w), 'days');
}
